prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can give names, but first: do you want only Dallas-based boutique firms, or are you okay with large national/regional plaintiff firms that handle Dallas cases? Also tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and a bit about the crash (injuries, whether a commercial truck was cited, police report) and I’ll tailor the list.

If you want a quick starter list to call now (national/regional firms that commonly handle truck-accident cases in Texas and either have Dallas offices or routinely take Dallas cases):

- Morgan & Morgan — large national plaintiffs’ firm with a Dallas presence. Why call: significant resources to handle big, complex truck cases (investigators, medical experts, reconstructionists), contingency-fee model, and experience litigating against large insurers and trucking companies.
- The Barnes Firm — national personal injury firm with a Dallas office. Why call: focused trial and settlement experience in serious vehicle and commercial-truck collisions, regular marketing presence in DFW and experience managing multi-million dollar claims.
- The Lanier Law Firm (Mark Lanier) — high-profile Texas trial lawyers who handle catastrophic injury and wrongful-death cases. Why call: strong trial reputation, experience trying large commercial-vehicle cases and obtaining large verdicts/settlements.
- Thomas J. Henry Law (Thomas J. Henry) — large Texas plaintiffs’ firm that handles serious truck crashes. Why call: experience with catastrophic injury cases, national reach, resources for reconstruction and expert witnesses.

Why these types of firms are worth calling
- Truck cases involve complex federal/state trucking regulations (FMCSA), black-box/ELDs, driver logs, maintenance and carrier liability — large firms more often have the investigators and experts to handle that complexity.
- Bigger insurers and trucking companies have experienced defense teams; having a firm with trial experience and resources puts pressure for fair settlement.

What to ask when you call (short script)
- “Do you handle commercial truck accidents in Dallas?” (Yes/no)
- “How many truck-accident cases have you handled in the last 3 years?”
- “Have you tried truck cases to verdict against carriers/insurers?” (ask for examples)
- “Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee/expense policy?”
- “Will you use accident reconstruction and FMCSA experts?” (ask about in-house vs. retained)
- “Who will handle my case day-to-day?” (attorney vs. paralegal)
- “Do you offer a free consultation and will you review the police report/medical records?”

Immediate practical steps for your case (do these now)
- Seek/continue medical care and keep all medical records.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles/scene/injuries, video if available, damaged property.
- Get the police report number and any citations.
- Do NOT give a recorded statement to the insurer without an attorney.
- Note witness names/contact info; save receipts and lost-wage proof.
- If possible, take screenshots of electronic logs (ELD) or ask the police if they will secure truck driver logs.

If you want, I can:
- Find specific Dallas boutique firms with strong truck-accident reputations and provide phone numbers/website links (tell me your ZIP or neighborhood), or
- Help you draft a 30–60 second script to use when calling firms or insurers.

Which would you prefer?
